comment: She is a nice person and her class isn't boring, but there are a few downsides. You will need to read 25-40 pages between each class and be able write about them. It was my most time-consuming class. I would only suggest taking her if you are specifically interested in the class. It is not worth it for a gen ed. lots of participation too.

She really did mean well, would make time to meet if you needed help, but would often not show up. Harsh grader expected a lot, but it was hard to get feedback from her because she missed meetings. But a really nice person, and was very passionate about the topic.

Professor Sackley is amazing. Her class is discussion-based, but if you are a student who cares about their writing and the material, she is always willing to help. She has sat with me and listened to me rant about other classes and has encouraged me to keep working hard because she sees potential in all people. Would def recommend for hist credit.

Dr. Sackley is SO smart and SO kind Her class is discussion based so make sure to do the readings! She brings snacks to class and is super understanding of how much work we have for other courses Grades are based on 2 papers (one 7ish pages and one 14ish), a practice writing assignment, partner presentation, participation, and a reflection paper

Very kind and caring. Very long readings that you need to keep up with because class is seminar style. You get a lot out of the class if you keep up with the homework. She is accessible outside of class and has clear grading criteria, so you'll do well if you put in the work

Requires a lot of reading, but her lectures are really interesting and she is genuinely the sweetest woman ever. I would take all of her classes if I could. I recommend this for people even if they aren't majoring in history
This class is a lot of work but you'll learn a lot.

Sackley is awesome. I took her Tobacco class and she was the best. We had no tests or quizzes, and had short readings, you're also assigned to watch a few movies. She takes this huge concept of tobacco, and dumbs and simplifies it down for you so that you understand it. Sackley the goat

Dr. Sackley wants to make her class a safe and welcoming environment, esp in light of recent incidents of racism on campus. Her class is reading heavy, but you will get so much out of her seminars if you read. She sees students as peers and values their contributions to discussion. Very kind and smart

Very interesting seminar but hard to participate if you don't read (very long! around 150-200 pages each week). Great professor, very engaging and warm, and makes discussions lively. I can see why other reviews say she's a tough grader but she does give constructive criticism so you can improve.

Professor Sackley is so nice and tough at the same time. I assume many of my classmates are taking this for their gen-ed, but this is not an intro-level difficulty class. Reading material is convoluted with tons of pages(at least 40 pages for every session). Participation matters a lot. Mid-term and final are very difficult.

So much reading for this class. She clearly understands her material but does not communicate that very well. The final is from hell, it is so unreasonable that I cannot comprehend how she thinks it can be done in 3 hours. As someone who is just trying to fill my history credit, I would not suggest at all.

She is a pretty tough grader and the criteria isn't always crystal clear but she will help you through any problems you have. Easily one of the most passionate and caring professors at UR. I would recommend.

Dr. Sackley is an absolutely phenomenal professor. In my four years at the University, I could not find a single professor comparable to her in terms of passion. She is an amazing professor and an even better person. The readings and discussion are a heavy load, but the satisfaction I got after leaving her class each week is insurmountable.

Good choice for general history electives. Knowledgeable about US history and great at choosing texts and readings for class. Lectures can be disorganized and she wasn't always the best at facilitating conversation; we occasionally got lost on what year we were talking about. Very reasonable work load, somewhat challenging but fair grader.  Nice.

She likes when you talk a lot in class and is willing to give you a break if you just talk to her. Papers and assignments aren't all that easy and there is a lot of reading you need to do for each class. She's very nice though. DO NOT TAKE if you have absolutely 0 interest in tobacco.. you will dread each class. Also, there's an all day field trip.

I took tobacco with her.  Make sure you participate and come to class prepared.  If you dont have your books she will ask you to leave.  Its an intensive reading class but if you keep up with it you will do well.  She is nice, bottom line, work for her and shell work for you.  Very nice and not intimidating even thought she is rediculously smart.
She is a great teacher. Take her class!

She's a really good professor. Very lively-walks all over class as shes talking. Must say that I really liked CORE b/c of her. Class participation is a big deal. She really wants us to share our thoughts and ideas with her. Grades very difficultly on her papers. VERY hard to get an A.

Dr. Sackley is a good teacher--recommend her to everyone not just majors.  Assigns a fair amount of reading and grades tough, but the class is always lively.  Helpful, understanding, will definitely work with you.  Down to earth, but knows her stuff.  Is younger/remembers what it's like to be an undergrad.

Professor Sackley is very interested and enthusiastic. She is nice and understanding and extremely helpful. She has a great sense of humor. Professor Sackley actually made Darwin and Nietzsche interesting! Core is one of my favorite classes.

Overall, very nice teacher. Very cheerful. Grades are hard. Most people get Bs or lower in her class. Very helpful (willing to see you at anytime pretty much). Must say that she is one of the better core teachers.
Dr. Sackley was extremely confusing as a professor.  No doubt she knows her material inside and out and her classes were marginally inspiring, but she lacked organization.

Professor Sackley is very fair with the amount of reading she assigns but some of the readings were kind of boring. She makes the class enjoyable and explains the dull readings to MAKE them interesting to you. Very accessible, friendly, and one of the better history professors at UR!

Very good teacher. Not a know-it-all so doesn't lecture much but very smart; puts onus on students to make class work. Very responsive via email and helpful in person. Haven't received final grade yet so don't know how tough she is. Changed some assignments at end of semester but generally well organized and fair with homework.
